To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PK activity can be considered a good indicator of the levels and the interactions of the cations K(+), Ca(2+), or Mg(2+) in cucumber plants grown in the greenhouse in calcareous soil.

the highest application of K in the calcareous soils used in this experiment reduced, in both leaves and fruits, foliar concentrations of both Mg(2+)and Ca(2+), resulting in the lowest basal PK activity and the highest differences in PK activities between basal and stimulated PK activities, indicating an imbalance between the different cationic concentrations in the leaves and fruit.

K(+) fertilizers applied to cucumber plants grown in calcareous soil have an important effect on the concentrations of Mg(+)2 and Ca(2 +), and on the activity of PK in both leaves and fruits, with the latter being an indicator of the former.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of K(+) on the PK activity in the leaves and fruit of cucumber grown in calcareous soil and the possible use of this enzyme activity as an indicator for K(+) fertilizers.
a new aspect of the role of PK activity in plants and its relationship with K(+) fertilizers in cucumber plants grown under calcareous soil conditions.
the possibility of using PK activity as an indicator in order to assess the level of cations in leaves and fruits and to optimize the use of K fertilization in greenhouse cultivation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the basal PK activity is a reliable indicator of the levels in the leaves of K(+), Ca(2+), Mg(2+) in cucumber plants grown in the greenhouse.
the PK activity is a good indicator of the level, in the leaves and the fruits, of K(+), Ca(2+), or Mg(2+) in cucumber plants.

the PK activity in the leaves and in the fruit is a reliable indicator of the levels and balance of the different cations in the culture media and that the highest K(+) application rate is not the most appropriate for the growth of cucumber in calcareous soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K(+) fertilized plants have higher yields and a better nutritional status.
PK activity in cucumber is a sensitive indicator of the levels and balance of the cations in cucumber leaves and fruits.
K fertilization in calcareous soil is beneficial and that the PK activity can be used as an indicator of cation balance in cucumber plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
K(+) fertilizers are important in the management of calcareous soils and that PK activity could be used as an indicator of K(+) nutrition in plants.
the activity of PK is a good indicator of the level, in the leaves and fruit of cucumber plants, of the cations K(+), Mg(+), and Ca(+) under the experimental conditions.
the PK activity is a good indicator of the levels and the balance of the three cations in the leaf and fruit tissue.
